Q561341.summary: At the centre of this jewelled gold cover Christ sits in majesty, raising his hand in blessing and holding an open book on his knee. Around him, embossed gold reliefs show the four evangelists, each with a scene from his Gospel, framed by raised settings of sapphires, emeralds and pearls. It is one of the very few treasure bindings to survive from the 9th century, a cover worthy of the King whom the Gospels proclaim.
facts: Wikipedia notes that the cover can be precisely dated to 870 and was made for Charles the Bald in his 'Palace School', whose location, perhaps Saint-Denis, is uncertain.
The book on Christ's knee is inscribed with his words 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life', so that the verse can be read as spoken by Christ or by the Gospel book itself.
The four scenes are Christ and the woman taken in adultery, the expulsion of the money-changers, the healing of the blind man and the healing of the leper.
